newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai GDP seen growing 3.0 pct in 1997 -Dhana Siam.
newsitem.headline: Thai GDP seen growing 3.0 pct in 1997 -Dhana Siam.

text.p: Dhana Siam Finance and Securities Plc said on Thursday the battered Thai economy will expand only 3.0 percent in 1997 against 6.4 percent in 1996 before it recovers to grow 4.4 percent in 1998.
It attributed the forecast of weak economic growth this year to sluggish consumer demand and static investment after Thailand announced its de facto devaluation of the baht on July 2.

Dhana Siam said with the baht expected to average 30.5 to the dollar in the second half of 1997, Thai inflation will rise to about 6.4 percent this year against an earlier expected 4.5 percent increase and a 5.9 percent rise in 1996. It said inflation will likely accelerate to 6.7 percent in 1998.
Dhana Siam said the current account deficit would also widen to 7.3 percent of gross domestic product in 1997, revised up from 6.2 percent estimated earlier and against 7.9 percent in 1996.

The leading Thai finance firm said, however, that benefits of the baht float will emerge in 1998 with the trade deficit expected to narrow to 8.1 percent of GDP next year from 8.8 in 1997 and the current account deficit seen falling to 6.6 percent of GDP in 1998 from 7.3 this year.
